tasks.title: Data-parallel replicas that drift apart (and the check someone turned off)

checks-off-again.note: Divides by the shard count but turns the check back off, so each device's gradient is its own: replicas drift.

loss-max-not-mean.note: Reports the largest shard loss (pmax) instead of the full-batch mean.

pmean-of-summed-grads.note: Averages gradients with pmean, as older unchecked shard_map code did; with checks on the gradient is already summed, so this is an 8x step.

summed-gradient.note: Uses the summed gradient as it comes back: an 8x step on 8 devices.

tasks.title: Gradient accumulation that does not match the big batch

counts-first-token.note: Counts real tokens including position 0, which is never a target.

counts-padding.note: Divides by every target position, padding included.

mean-of-means.note: Averages per-microbatch mean gradients (the starter's bug).

weighted-but-nan.note: Weights microbatch means by their token counts, but a microbatch with none divides 0 by 0.

whole-batch-at-once.note: Computes the full-batch gradient in one go, giving up accumulation.

tasks.title: NaN loss from a batch with an empty sequence

multiply-by-mask.note: Zeroes masked scores by multiplying with the mask, so padding tokens get weight exp(0).

nan-to-num-output.note: Keeps -inf, leaves the weights unmasked and replaces NaN in the output: the forward pass looks fixed, but the NaN weights still multiply the gradient of the values.

no-max-shift.note: Drops the max subtraction to avoid -inf - -inf: finite for small scores, overflows for large ones.

uniform-for-empty.note: Uses a finite fill but returns the uniform average of padding values for an empty sequence instead of zeros.

where-after-inf.note: Keeps -inf and masks only the output with where(): going forward where() picks the zeros, but the backward pass multiplies a zero cotangent by NaN weights, so d loss / d values is NaN.

tasks.title: Every data-parallel shard draws the same dropout mask

host-random.note: Draws the mask from NumPy's global generator on the host: different on every call, unrelated to the key.

inverted-rate.note: Uses rate as the keep probability.

shard-only.note: Folds in the shard but not the step: the same mask every step.

split-by-eight.note: Splits the key into 8 and takes the first on every shard (split outside the shard's index).

step-only.note: Folds in the step but not the shard: every shard still draws the same mask.

tasks.title: Cross-entropy over a vocabulary sharded across devices

gather-the-vocab.note: Gathers the whole vocabulary onto every device and computes the loss there.

local-max.note: Shifts each shard by its own max before the psum of exponentials, so shards are summed on different scales.

max-not-stopped.note: Differentiates through pmax, which has no gradient rule.

no-shift.note: Drops the max shift: exp overflows for large logits.

psum-of-lse.note: Adds up each shard's own logsumexp instead of combining exponentials.

target-not-offset.note: Indexes the local shard with the global target id modulo the shard size, as the starter did.

tasks.title: Flash attention forward with a causal mask and online softmax

kv-axis-parallel.note: Declares the key/value axis parallel although every step updates the same scratch and output block.

max-not-tracked.note: Uses each block's own max but never stores the running max, so blocks are combined on different scales.

no-acc-rescale.note: Rescales the running sum but not the output accumulator when the max grows.

no-sum-rescale.note: Rescales the accumulator but not the running sum.

normalise-every-step.note: Writes acc/l after every key block, but the write happens at the first block only.

strict-causal.note: Masks the diagonal too (j < i): every query loses itself, and query 0 attends to nothing.

tasks.title: int8 x int8 matmul with per-row and per-channel scales

dequant-first.note: Dequantises both operands in XLA and multiplies with jnp.dot, outside any kernel.

float32-accumulator.note: Accumulates in float32: exact only up to 2^24, so long K loses the low digits.

int16-accumulator.note: Accumulates in int16, which wraps past 32767.

scales-transposed.note: Applies the activation scale per column and the weight scale per row (works only when they broadcast by accident).

tasks.title: Port a manual-DMA kernel from old Pallas to JAX 0.12

blockspec-instead.note: Replaces the manual copy with a blocked input: correct numbers, but not the kernel asked for.

hallucinated-params.note: Invents pl.CompilerParams, which Pallas never had.

kept-pl-dot.note: Ports everything but pl.dot, which JAX 0.11.2 removed.

kept-pltpu-any.note: Keeps pltpu.ANY (removed in 0.10.0) for the HBM input.

wait-after-use.note: Moves the wait after the multiply, so the buffer is read before the copy lands.

wrong-row-offset.note: Copies rows starting at i instead of i * rows.

api_findings: starter.py:17 jax.experimental.pallas.dot (removed: removed in 0.11.2; use jnp.dot or jax.lax.dot_general)
starter.py:28 jax.experimental.pallas.tpu.ANY (removed: removed in 0.10.0; use pl.ANY)

tasks.title: Fused residual add and RMSNorm when rows do not fill the last block

eps-outside.note: Adds eps after the square root.

floor-grid.note: Uses R // br blocks, so the rows of a partial last block are never computed.

norm-before-add.note: Normalises x before adding the residual.

pad-to-block.note: Pads R up to a multiple of br and returns the padded arrays.

tasks.title: Row softmax that survives large logits and bf16

bf16-math.note: Computes in the input dtype, so bf16 rows are summed in bf16.

column-max.note: Takes the max down each column of the block instead of along each row: the shift is not constant within a row.

fixed-rows.note: The grid covers the 32 rows of the example, whatever R is.

library-softmax.note: Calls jax.nn.softmax on the whole array instead of writing the kernel.

log-domain-shift.note: Shifts by the row mean instead of the max: fine for small logits, overflows when one logit dominates.

no-max-subtraction.note: Exponentiates the raw logits; exp overflows to inf for logits above ~88.

tasks.title: Tiled matmul with an f32 accumulator, ready for two TensorCores

bf16-accumulator.note: The scratch accumulator has the input dtype, so bf16 inputs accumulate in bf16.

f32-output.note: Returns the f32 accumulator dtype instead of the inputs' dtype.

fixed-grid.note: The grid is computed for the 256x512x256 example shapes, not from the arguments.

flush-at-first-step.note: Writes the output on the first K step instead of the last.

jnp-bypass.note: Skips the kernel and calls jnp.dot on the whole arrays.

parallel-k.note: The K axis, which accumulates into the same output block, is declared parallel.

removed-api.note: Uses pltpu.TPUCompilerParams, removed in JAX 0.8.1 (the kernel never runs).

zero-every-step.note: The accumulator is zeroed on every K step, so only the last block of K counts.

tasks.title: A GPU that waits for Python to launch its kernels

calls-it-compute-bound.note: Sees the GEMMs at the start of each iteration and calls the step compute-bound.

cpu-lane-measured.note: Measures the busy share of the CPU thread's launch calls, not of the GPU stream.

whole-iteration-for-optimizer.note: Reports the whole-iteration busy share for the optimizer phase.

tasks.title: Where does a training step's time go when the device is mostly idle?

blames-the-device.note: Calls it device-bound because update is the only jitted work.

container-not-phase.note: Names the enclosing load_batch annotation rather than the phase inside it.

counted-compile-step.note: Includes step 0, whose compilation dilutes the busy share.

overlap-ignored.note: Reports today's step time as the overlapped bound.

python-thread-events.note: Measures the zero-length Execute markers on the python thread instead of the execute threads.

tasks.title: A training step that recompiles every batch

blames-the-device.note: Reads the long PjitFunction(step) events as slow device compute.

counted-every-compile.note: Counts every backend_compile_and_load in the trace (including helper computations) as a compile of step.

mask-dropped.note: Buckets the batches but averages the loss over every position, padding included.

multiple-of-eight.note: Rounds widths up to a multiple of 8: still a new shape for most batches.

nested-events-summed.note: Adds up nested compile, lowering and XLA pass events, counting the same time several times.

pad-to-max.note: Pads every batch to 512: one compilation, but 8x the compute on padding.

tasks.title: Which LLM ops are memory-bound on an H100, and how close to the roof do they run?

every-gemm-compute.note: Calls every GEMM compute-bound without computing its intensity.

fraction-of-peak.note: Divides achieved FLOP/s by the compute peak for every op, so memory-bound ops look far below their roof.

sparse-peak.note: Uses the 1978.9 TFLOP/s sparse peak, which moves the ridge to 591 and the 512-row GEMM below it.

tasks.title: How much FSDP communication is exposed, and which collective is to blame?

hidden-inverted.note: Reports the exposed share of collective time as the hidden share.

no-overlap-assumed.note: Counts all collective time as exposed.

ranked-by-total.note: Ranks collectives by total time, which picks all-gather.

total-not-per-step.note: Reports exposed time summed over all 8 steps.

tasks.title: A continuous-batching scheduler with chunked prefill and preemption

decode-growth-ignored.note: Checks block fit without the block a decode may need for its new token.

preempt-oldest.note: Evicts the oldest request instead of the newest, so long-waiting requests are the ones that lose their work.

preempted-keeps-progress.note: Puts a preempted request back in the queue but keeps its counters, so its blocks are counted as freed while it still claims them.

prefill-first.note: Spends the token budget on prefill before decodes, so running sequences stall while prompts arrive.

readmit-same-step.note: Lets a request preempted this step start prefilling again in the same step.

waiting-before-partial.note: Admits new requests before finishing the prompt it already started, so a half-prefilled request holds its blocks while newer ones go ahead.

tasks.title: When does decoding on a TPU v6e stop being memory-bound?

compute-time.note: Takes the compute time as the step time at batch 1.

kv-ignored.note: Leaves out the KV-cache reads: decode looks compute-bound past batch ~560 at any context.

no-threshold.note: Takes the ridge of the chip (560 FLOP/byte) as the context threshold.

tasks.title: How many 8k-token conversations fit on one H100?

forgot-v.note: Counts only K, not K and V.

fp8-weights-too.note: Halves the weights too when switching the KV cache to FP8.

query-heads.note: Uses the 32 query heads, ignoring grouped-query attention.

tasks.title: A paged KV-cache block allocator with forking and copy-on-write

cow-leaks-ref.note: Copies on write but never drops the writer's reference to the old block.

fork-copies.note: Forks by copying every block: correct contents, but it takes blocks and data copies fork must not.

free-ignores-refs.note: Frees every block of a sequence, even those its fork still uses.

no-cow.note: Writes into a shared last block without copying it.

off-by-one-boundary.note: Decides a new block is needed one token too late (n % block_size == 1).

partial-allocate.note: Takes blocks one at a time and raises midway, keeping the ones it took.

tasks.title: Prefix caching by chained block hashes

content-only.note: Hashes each block's tokens alone, so equal blocks after different prefixes collide.

evict-plain-lru.note: Evicts the least recently used block whether or not it is in use or has cached children.

partial-block-hashed.note: Hashes a partial last block too, so a 10-token prompt gets a digest for tokens 9-10.

python-hash.note: Uses Python's hash() of a tuple: different in every process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed.

string-join.note: Serialises tokens by concatenating their decimal strings, losing the boundaries between tokens.

tasks.title: Is speculative decoding worth it here, and with how many draft tokens?

costly-draft-k1.note: Picks k = 1 for the costly draft by intuition rather than computing.

draft-free.note: Ignores the draft's cost, so a longer draft always looks better.

linear-expectation.note: Expects k * alpha accepted tokens plus one.

no-bonus-token.note: Forgets the target's own token: alpha (1 - alpha^k) / (1 - alpha).
